thread:
anna: Quick sync — need a decision on two Q3 initiatives: 'batch prefetch / KV prefix caching' vs 'dedicated burst autoscale'. Both reduce tail latency for bursty workloads but have different effort and cross-team work. Can we use a lightweight RICE + a temporary staff swap to pick sequencing?

raj: Can you share rough expected impact numbers? who are the customer asks driving this? :thinking:

mike: Engineering constraints: runtime can land a basic prefix cache + metrics in ~3 weeks if we allocate ~0.5 FTE (engineer) focused for 6 sprints. Autoscale (node-level burst pools + scheduler changes) looks like ~8–10 weeks + infra testing. Autoscale also needs infra hooks for warm pools.

sofia: Customer signal: HealthCorp and one fintech pilot asked for better behavior on 20–40% traffic spikes. HealthCorp called this a blocker for their go-live. So there is near-term revenue risk if spikes blow past p95.

jess: Ok quick RICE sketch to make this concrete. keep in mind Reach = fraction of affected calls per month.

```
Batch cache:
Reach=0.3, Impact=3 (noticeable p50/p95), Confidence=0.7, Effort=2 (low)
RICE = (0.3 * 3 * 0.7) / 2 = 0.315

Autoscale:
Reach=0.5, Impact=2 (handles more customers but less per-request quality)
Confidence=0.6, Effort=5 (high)
RICE = (0.5 * 2 * 0.6) / 5 = 0.12
```

sofia: Those numbers track with customer asks. Cache is a quick win for HealthCorp. Autoscale is more of a systemic improvement for large multi-tenant customers.

raj: My read: do cache first as a canary-friendly win, then schedule autoscale in the next quarter. Sequencing note: cache reduces load and buys time to design autoscale properly.

mike: Agree. One infra dependency though: platform needs to expose eviction/usage metrics (1 week of infra work) so we can measure cache efficacy and set rollout gates. If product approves, I can take the 0.5 FTE from our backlog for 6 sprints — but we need a test harness from product (small perf test suite).

anna: Actionable proposal: 1) Ship prefix cache as Q3 sprint focus (owner: mike). 2) Allocate 0.5 FTE from eng-platform to runtime for the next 6 sprints. 3) infra (eng-infra) to add eviction/usage metrics by EOW. 4) Autoscale moved to Q4 planning; create a spec doc with costs and safety fallbacks.

jess: Suggested launch criteria for cache rollout:
- p50 improved by >= 15% on bursty routes (measured in canary)
- p95 not regress > 5%
- no error-rate increase > 0.1%
- cost delta (tokens/sec infra) < 5%
- runbook + fallback (toggle off) verified in staging

mike: I can target a staged rollout with a 5% canary for HealthCorp traffic, then 25%, then full. Will need a quick A/B harness; product to provide test prompt set.

sofia: I'll coordinate with HealthCorp success to get a representative prompt set and confirm acceptance criteria. Also will flag revenue impact to prioritize infra work.

raj: On the staff-swap: agree to temporary 0.5 FTE shift if product commits to the perf harness and we freeze scope to the MVP cache (no extra features). Please document the scope cut.

anna: I'll create a short spec PR with scope, timeline, and the RICE calc above. If everyone OK, I'll add to the sprint plan and ping eng-infra for the 1-week metric work. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: scheduled: deploy-checklist created for "prefix-cache-mvp" (staging) — CI pipeline will run perf-harness once harness PR is linked.

jess: Sounds good. Small ask: let's record the RICE inputs in the ticket so future reviewers know the assumptions.

anna: Yep, will add the numbers and owners. Thanks all — will update after I open the spec PR. :rocket:
